title: NIAMS says a newborn has about 300 bones and a grown person has 206
summary: NIAMS says a newborn has about 300 bones, and many later fuse into the 206 bones of a grown person.
body: The NIAMS bones page says a newborn has about 300 bones. Many of them eventually fuse, which the page calls growing together, forming the 206 bones of a grown person. About 300 is the page figure, not an exact census of one newborn. The 206 is the count on that page. Fusion during childhood is the claim. The page is a US school resource, not a count from every anatomy book.

sources.title: Health Lesson: Learning About Bones
sources.author: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
sources.note: US government page, public domain. Last Updated June 2025. Did You Know box: a baby is born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse to form the 206 adult bones.
